theorem regret_comparison (V : Domain (E := E)) (A : LinearPolicy (E := E)) (loss : ℕ → E → EReal) (p : SupportPolicy (E := E)) (T : ℕ) (hloss : ∀ t < T, BanditRL.OnlineSubgradientDescent.SubdifferentiableOn V (loss t)) (hlegal : LegalFeedback A loss p T) (u : E) (hu : u ∈ V.carrier) :

    regret A loss p u T ≤ BanditRL.OnlineLearning.comparatorRegret (fun t => linearLoss (selected A loss p t)) (linearRun A (selected A loss p)) u T := by
  unfold regret
  rw [BanditRL.OnlineLearning.comparatorRegret_eq_sum]
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro t ht
  rw [linearLoss_gap, ← output_linear_run A loss p t]
  exact support_gap V (loss t) (hloss t (Finset.mem_range.mp ht))

comparisons.blind_boundary: This type alone does not require subgradient membership or causality beyond its supplied argument shape.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Alias of whole-loss finite-history support policy type; no global validity in the type.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.Feasible
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: A(t,h) belongs to V.carrier for all histories.
comparisons.blind_boundary: This quantifies all vector histories, not merely histories arising from admissible losses.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal all-times/all-histories feasibility predicate.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.outputHistory
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Entry i, whose natural value is k<=t, is A(k, j -> h(j)) using only h at j<k. It reconstructs decisions 0 through t.
comparisons.blind_boundary: The elided field is a proof that j<k<=t, not a missing mathematical hypothesis. No actual loss sequence is needed.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal prefix reconstruction including current output; bounded-index omega proof is typing only.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.history
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: H_0 is the unique function with empty domain. H_(t+1) appends p(t, losses at indices below t, Q05(A,H_t), loss(t)) to H_t.
comparisons.blind_boundary: The appended value need not be a subgradient absent additional validity assumptions. The current loss is consulted for feedback after the current decision has been reconstructed.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal well-founded natural recursion, appending current selected vector after current output is reconstructed.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.output
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: x_t=A(t,H_t).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Only vector feedback before time t enters A. Feasibility requires a separate hypothesis.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal application A t to actual recursive history.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.selected
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: g_t=p(t, earlier full loss functions, Q05(A,H_t), loss(t)).
comparisons.blind_boundary: The provider sees the current loss and decisions through time t. It need not be globally valid.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal p application to actual past whole losses, reconstructed outputs through t, and current whole loss.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.LegalFeedback
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: For each t<T, g_t belongs to S_(loss(t))(x_t).
comparisons.blind_boundary: This is a finite-horizon assumption/property, not D08 universal validity. It is vacuous for T=0.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal played-prefix global supporting inequality membership, no properness bundled here.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.linearRun
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: P_A(g,t)=A(t, i -> g(i)), where i:Fin t.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Uses g only strictly before t. No loss functions or provider are involved.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal application of the same A to prefixes of an externally supplied vector sequence.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.linearLoss
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q11(g,x)=inner_R(g,x), a real number.
comparisons.blind_boundary: This is a linear functional, without an affine offset or EReal coercion in its output.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal real inner product, no affine offset.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.regret
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Sum for t=0,...,T-1 of toReal(loss(t,x_t))-toReal(loss(t,u)). Comparator u is fixed.
comparisons.blind_boundary: No feasibility/admissibility is built into the definition; infinite losses map to zero under toReal. Empty sum at T=0 is zero.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal sum of toReal differences. Finite-value hypotheses are needed to identify it with source regret.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.outputHistory_last
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q05(A,h)(last t)=A(t,h). The index last t has natural value t.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Identity for arbitrary histories; no feasibility or loss assumptions.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Definitional equality: the last output uses the full prior-vector function; subtype proof irrelevance does not change vector values.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.history_zero
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: H_0 equals Fin.elim0 as functions on Fin 0.
comparisons.blind_boundary: No nonempty time step and no provider validity premise.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Definitional Nat.rec base, unique function on Fin 0.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.history_succ
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: H_(t+1)=Fin.snoc(H_t,g_t).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Appends the feedback at time t, not the decision at time t.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Definitional Nat.rec step appends the actual selected vector, not a surrogate assumed later.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.history_castSucc
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: H_(t+1)(i.castSucc)=H_t(i).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Only the old-index case; it does not itself state the value at the new last index.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Uses history_succ and Fin.snoc_castSucc, preserving each old coordinate.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.history_selected
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: H_t(i)=g_(natural value of i).
comparisons.blind_boundary: The allowed index is strictly below t.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Induction on t, Fin.lastCases separates newly appended support from inherited coordinates; old case uses history_castSucc.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.output_linear_run
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: x_t=P_A(g,t) for the induced entire sequence g=Q08(A,loss,p).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Equality of decisions, without an admissibility, regret or provider-validity claim.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Unfolds both outputs, extensional equality of input histories via history_selected. Same A and same actual selected sequence.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.outputHistory_played
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q05(A,H_t)(i)=x_(natural value of i), including i=t.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Includes current decision and previous decisions, unlike H_t which contains only prior feedback.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Expands reconstructed history and actual output, then uses history_selected on both prefixes. Includes current output without current support.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.output_mem
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: x_t belongs to V.carrier.
comparisons.blind_boundary: No admissibility or global/trajectory provider validity is needed.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Applies universal Feasible A to the actual finite history; no loss or support legality used.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.history_prefix
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: H_t(A,loss,p)=H_t(A,loss_prime,p).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Uses the same A and p. Does not assert equal feedback at t when current losses differ, or invariance under equality only at visited points.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Induction rewrites previous feedback history, the entire prior-loss function tuple, and current loss at the extension step. Fixed A and p throughout. No equality at current t required in final H_t.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.output_prefix
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: x_t(A,loss,p)=x_t(A,loss_prime,p).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Current/future losses may differ. This is deterministic prefix invariance, not stochastic independence.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Congruence of the same A t applied to history_prefix. No independence/randomness statement.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.oracle_feedback
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q09(A,loss,p,T) holds.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Requires provider validity for arbitrary inputs through D08, although the conclusion concerns only this trajectory and horizon.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Constructs feasibility of last reconstructed output from outputHistory_last and hA, then applies the all-context hp to the actual past losses/history/current loss and hloss.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.canonical_feedback
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q09(A,loss,D09,T).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Uses the classical selector and the supplied context D12. Does not certify an executable oracle.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Instantiates oracle_feedback with canonicalPolicy_legal; no separate legal-feedback premise is assumed.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.trajectory_finite_loss
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: loss(t,x_t)=coerce(toReal(loss(t,x_t))).
comparisons.blind_boundary: No D08 or Q09 premise is needed because universal feasibility keeps x_t in V. No statement about t>=T.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Uses output_mem and upstream finite_loss. This feasible-path helper is not the producer needed by the ambient core comparison.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.support_gap
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: toReal(f(x))-toReal(f(u)) <= inner(g,x-u).
comparisons.blind_boundary: There is no x in V hypothesis. Finiteness of f(u) follows from admissibility on V; properness rules out f(x)=-infinity and the supporting inequality at a finite point rules out f(x)=+infinity. This justifies toReal even for x outside V.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Applies actual lemma_2_31 at eta=1 and selects first conjunct. Upstream subgradient_point_finite proves x finite without x∈V; hf.2 supplies support at u and hence u finite. Coercions are justified before real subtraction. Projection second conjunct is unused in the conclusion.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.linearLoss_gap
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q11(g,x)-Q11(g,u)=inner(g,x-u).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Exact real linearity identity; no inequality, convexity, or bound on norms.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Exact inner_sub_right symmetry. No convexity/norm bound is assumed.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.regret_comparison
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q12(A,loss,p,u,T) <= D05(t -> Q11(g_t), P_A(g), u,T). The right side is sum_{t<T} inner(g_t,x_t-u), using T06.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Does not assume Q04 or D08. Only the trajectory memberships are required; actions may be outside V. No convergence rate or stochastic guarantee is supplied.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Rewrites comparatorRegret as sum of differences, applies sum_le_sum, rewrites linearLoss_gap and actual output_linear_run, and applies support_gap with hloss and hlegal at each actual t<T.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.regret_transfer
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q12(A,loss,p,u,T)<=B(Q08(A,loss,p),u,T).
comparisons.blind_boundary: B may depend on the entire g sequence, u and T. Its assumed guarantee is universal in g at the already fixed T, not an assumption universally quantified over all horizons. No Q04/D08 or numerical rate is inserted.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Transitivity of actual regret_comparison and hB instantiated at selected A loss p, same u,T,A. Universal linear bound is a supplied producer contract, not an assumed convex-regret inequality.

comparisons.name: BanditRL.OnlineLinearization.canonical_regret_comparison
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q12(A,loss,D09,u,T) <= linear regret of the D09-induced vector sequence replayed through A at the same u,T.
comparisons.blind_boundary: No separately assumed Q09 is needed. Both sides use the same canonical-induced sequence, not the explicit example provider.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Composes regret_comparison with canonical_feedback; both sides contain the same canonical-induced sequence.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.V
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Carrier is Set.univ, supplied with nonempty, closed and convex certificates.
comparisons.blind_boundary: The certificate bodies are not given and are not reviewed here. This set is unbounded.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Unbounded real-line domain with explicit nonempty/closed/convex certificates.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.learner
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: A(t,h)=-sum_{i:Fin t} h(i). In particular A(0,empty)=0.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Unit coefficient, with no division by time, projection, clipping, or positive regularizer parameter in the definition.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal negative sum of past feedback, coefficient1, no projection or averaging.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.quadratic
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: f_0(x)=coerce((x-1)^2/2) in EReal.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Finite everywhere, centered at 1, with coefficient 1/2.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal finite loss (x-1)^2/2 embedded in EReal.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.affine
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: f_+(x)=coerce(x) in EReal.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Finite everywhere; slope 1. It is not bounded below on Q13.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal finite linear loss x embedded in EReal.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.losses
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: At t=0 use Q15; at every t!=0 use Q16.
comparisons.blind_boundary: The second branch covers all positive times, not only t=1.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Quadratic at0, affine at all positive times.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.policy
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: At t=0 output h(last t)-1; at every t!=0 output 1. Previous losses and the current loss argument are ignored.
comparisons.blind_boundary: It is not a globally D08-valid provider for arbitrary admissible current losses. T30 only establishes trajectory validity for Q17 through T=2. With the zero loss at t=1, output 1 violates its subgradient inequality at y=x+1.
comparisons.independent_assessment: At0 current output minus1, otherwise1. Ignores past/current losses; valid on this chosen trajectory but fails OracleLaw for arbitrary admissible current losses.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.x
comparisons.blind_boundary: An alias of the explicit-provider trajectory, distinct from the D09-induced trajectory in T41.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Alias of actual explicit-policy output.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.g
comparisons.blind_boundary: The definition makes feedback -1 at 0 and 1 at positive times once x_0=0 is evaluated. It is not a separate exogenous random process.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Alias of actual explicit-policy selected feedback.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.learner_feasible
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q04(Q13,Q14): all decisions from arbitrary real feedback histories lie in R=Q13.carrier.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Feasibility in the whole real line imposes no boundedness.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Every real action belongs to univ; does not prove boundedness.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.quadratic_support
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: z-1 belongs to S_Q15(z), meaning for every y:R, (z-1)^2/2+(z-1)(y-z) <= (y-1)^2/2.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Exact residual is (y-z)^2/2. Membership does not itself assert uniqueness of the subgradient.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Coerces finite real values, normalizes real inner product, and uses sq_nonneg(y-z) to prove the exact quadratic support residual.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.affine_support
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: 1 belongs to S_Q16(z), since z+1*(y-z)=y for every y.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Equality holds in the supporting inequality. No bounded loss assumption.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Coerces finite values and simplifies z+(y-z)=y; slope 1 is a global support.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.quadratic_on
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: D04(Q13,Q15): Q15 never equals -infinity, has a finite real witness, and has at least one ambient subgradient at every real point.
comparisons.blind_boundary: No optimization-rate conclusion.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Constructs properness explicitly with witness x=0,value=1/2, never-bottom, and support z-1 at each z.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.affine_on
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: D04(Q13,Q16), with all function values finite and subgradient 1 everywhere.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Admissibility does not require a minimizer or a lower bound over Q13.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Constructs properness with witness x=0,value=0, never-bottom, and support1 at each z. No minimizer needed.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.losses_on
comparisons.blind_boundary: Unlike T30, this proposition is not limited to a two-round horizon.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Cases on t=0 and reuses quadratic_on or affine_on. All natural times, not merely T=2.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.x_zero
comparisons.blind_boundary: Time index 0 precedes any feedback.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Unfolds the learner on the empty history; sum is zero.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.g_zero
comparisons.blind_boundary: Feedback at time 0 is used to form the decision at time 1.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Uses outputHistory_last at t=0, empty-history learner=0, then subtracts1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.g_one
comparisons.blind_boundary: Only this index is stated, even though the definition fixes every positive-time output to 1.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Unfolds selected and explicit policy at positive time; output is exactly1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.x_one
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q19(1)=1, the negative of the sole previous feedback -1.
comparisons.blind_boundary: This decision is made before applying the linear loss at time 1.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Replays actual g through output_linear_run and the one-element finite sum; g0=-1 yields1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.x_two
comparisons.blind_boundary: This is the terminal decision for horizon 2 and is not a summand decision in a range 2 loss sum.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Replays actual g through output_linear_run; g0=-1,g1=1 yield0.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.feedback_two
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q09(Q14,Q17,Q18,2), so g_0=-1 is a subgradient at x_0=0 and g_1=1 is a subgradient at x_1=1.
comparisons.blind_boundary: This proposition does not assert global provider validity D08 or explicitly quantify other horizons.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Splits t<2 into0 or1; uses actual g and x values plus quadratic_support/affine_support. No OracleLaw is assumed or proved.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_same_linear_run
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q19(1)=Q10(Q14,Q20,1), both equal to 1.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Only time 1 is stated here; the general replay equality is T06.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Direct real consumer of output_linear_run at1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_convex_regret
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q12(Q14,Q17,Q18,1,2)=1/2. The t=0 difference is 1/2-0 and the t=1 difference is 1-1=0.
comparisons.blind_boundary: This is an exact deterministic regret, not expected regret or average regret.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Expands exact two summands using actual outputs and finite losses; yields1/2.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_linear_regret
comparisons.blind_boundary: The loss is linearized with the actual feedback sequence and replayed decisions.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Rewrites comparatorRegret_eq_sum and same-run equality, evaluates actual supports/actions; yields1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_public_comparison
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Nonlinear regret <= linearized regret, numerically 1/2<=1.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Does not assert equality or a separately optimized comparator.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Actual application of public regret_comparison with independently established losses_on and feedback_two, not a rewritten numerical tautology.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_strict_slack
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Nonlinear regret < linearized regret, numerically 1/2<1.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Strict slack is 1/2, arising from the quadratic at time 0. Thus this is a nondegenerate reduction example.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Uses exact actual_convex_regret and actual_linear_regret then proves1/2<1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.bound
comparisons.blind_boundary: The negative terminal squared-distance term is retained. Q10 uses the decision after all T earlier feedback values. The definition itself is for all T, but T36 below states an identity only at T=2.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Literal initial potential plus half energy minus terminal potential; defined allT, proved universally in vectors/comparators only atT2.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.universal_two
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: D05(t -> Q11(v(t)),Q10(Q14,v),u,2)=Q21(v,u,2). With a=v(0),b=v(1), both sides equal -a*b-u*(a+b).
comparisons.blind_boundary: Universal in v,u, not a single-instance calculation. No restriction on vector sizes. The theorem does not quantify T, despite the expression being defined for arbitrary T.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Unfolds arbitrary vector sequence v and arbitrary comparator u at horizon2; ring normalizes both sides to -v0*v1-u*(v0+v1). Negative terminal term retained.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_public_transfer
comparisons.blind_boundary: Uses the complete expression including its negative terminal term.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Actual public regret_transfer consumer; universal_two(v,u).le supplies hB for every v,u. Uses actual legality, not OracleLaw.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.actual_bound_value
comparisons.blind_boundary: Dropping the negative term would give 3/2 and would not match this equality.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Obtains terminal replay=0 from output_linear_run and x_two; computes 1/2+2/2-1/2=1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.nonzero_energy
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Sum_{t in range 2} Q20(t)^2=2, from (-1)^2+1^2.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Both time indices 0 and 1 contribute; this is not a norm of the sum.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Evaluates g0²+g1²=2, not squared sum.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.positive_terminal
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Norm(Q19(2)-1)^2=1, since Q19(2)=0 and the real norm is absolute value.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Terminal index is 2 and comparator is 1. The subtracted term in Q21 is this value divided by 2.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Rewrites x2=0 and evaluates real norm of -1 squared=1.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.canonical_producer_instance
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q12(Q14,Q17,D09,1,2) <= linear regret for g_t=Q08(Q14,Q17,D09,t), replayed via Q10(Q14,g), at u=1,T=2.
comparisons.blind_boundary: Both sides use D09. This statement does not explicitly identify its choices with Q18 or assert either side has the numeric values in T32/T33. Choice membership follows supplied context, not a newly certified Lean proof.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Actual canonical_regret_comparison consumer with learner_feasible and losses_on; does not identify the canonical trajectory with explicit policy values.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.invalid_future
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: At t=0 use Q17(0)=Q15. At every t!=0 use the constant EReal +infinity function.
comparisons.blind_boundary: At positive times D01 fails because there is no finite real witness. It is therefore not D04-admissible, even though the constant +infinity function has every vector in D02 at every point. Arbitrary toReal regret would collapse these infinite values to zero.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Original loss at0 and constant top from1 onward; fails finite-witness properness at positive times.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.current_and_future_do_not_change_output
comparisons.blind_reconstruction: Q07(Q14,Q22,Q18,1)=1. Time-0 loss is unchanged, so feedback history before time 1 remains [-1].
comparisons.blind_boundary: The current time-1 loss is +infinity and inadmissible. This is a prefix-causality example only, not an admissible infinite-loss reduction theorem.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Uses output_prefix from losses to invalid_future at1; only index0 equality required, then x_one. Proves prediction only, not admissibility or finite regret of the top-valued tail.

comparisons.name: LinearizationProbe.zero_horizon_actual_comparison
comparisons.blind_boundary: All sums are empty. This is a boundary check, not the nondegenerate strict example T35.
comparisons.independent_assessment: Uses public regret_comparison at0; hloss/hlegal discharged by impossible t<0, both empty sums. This does not substitute for the nondegenerate two-round consumer.
